description: The bar chart illustrates the effect of context masking on case tasks grouped by language family, with error bars indicating the standard deviation for each measurement. The horizontal category axis, labeled "family," displays nine language families arranged in alphabetical order: IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic. The vertical value axis, labeled "effect," uses a linear scale ranging from slightly below zero to 35, with numeric tick labels placed at intervals of 10 (0, 10, 20, and 30) and corresponding horizontal grid lines extending across the plot. The chart features grouped bars, where each language family contains a cluster of six adjacent bars representing different models as indicated by the legend: mBERT-L₂ (light blue), XLM-L₂ (dark blue), mBERT-R₂ (light green), XLM-R₂ (dark green), mBERT-B₂ (light pink), and XLM-B₂ (dark red). All bars are outlined in black and are visually annotated with vertical error bars capped with horizontal lines. The tallest bars are observed in the IE-Indic group, where mBERT-B₂ reaches a peak approximate value of 24, followed by XLM-B₂ at roughly 21 and mBERT-R₂ at 20. The Semitic group also contains prominently tall bars, notably XLM-B₂ near 19 and XLM-L₂ near 16. Conversely, the shortest bars, including several that dip into negative values, are found in the IE-Germanic, Semitic, Isolate, and Uralic groups; for example, the mBERT-R₂ and XLM-R₂ bars in the Semitic group extend downward to approximately -2.5 and -1.5, respectively. The Isolate and Uralic clusters consist entirely of very short bars with values hovering near zero, generally remaining below 2. The bars within each grouping maintain the consistent six-model order defined in the legend.
